title: Comprehensive Guide to Maintaining 75mm Ribbed Tubing for Extended Lifespan in Drip Irrigation Systems
html:
Introduction to the Importance of 75 mm Water Transfer Pipes

In modern drip and tape irrigation systems, main and branch pipes play a vital role in the uniform delivery of water. 75 mm diameter pipes (which often feature threaded connections for joining to laterals) are a popular choice for orchards and greenhouses due to their suitable operating pressure and flexibility. However, as is common with any industrial equipment, an unmonitored pipe can suffer from abrasion, connection leaks, or even rupture after a few seasons. The objective of this article is to provide a comprehensive checklist of Maintenance of 75 mm Threaded Pipes so that you can predict how to extend the useful life of these costly assets. This guide is written for irrigation engineers and practical growers.

To better understand how these pipes integrate with other components, we recommend also reading the article on the domain of determining tape irrigation emitters locations, as the correct placement of start points reduces pressure on the main line.

Why are 75 mm Pipes Vulnerable to Damage?

  • Mechanical movement caused by the rotation of cranes and machinery
  • Vibration and severe temperature changes that cause fitting contraction and expansion
  • Water chemical composition that may cause corrosion of metal components or deterioration of the gasket
  • Ultraviolet (UV) radiation if the pipe is not properly buried

Fundamentals of correct installation

Most complaints regarding Maintenance of 75 mm threaded pipe It starts from the installation stage. If the pipe is not in the proper trench, thermal stress increases. Always ensure an appropriate distance between the bottom of the trench and the pipe (40 to 50 cm deep depending on the region). The gasket layer of soft sand must be smooth and free of gravel.

Additional tips regarding connections

Threaded connections require proper PTFE tape and correct adhesion. The use of unsuitable industrial adhesives can cause pipe rupture during disassembly. For general layout principles, refer to the Arifouzi blue-type Tarofoz guide.

Scheduled Cleaning and Flushing Program

One of the most important aspects of maintenance for the 75 mm threaded pipeis regular flushing. Mineral deposits and algae settle on the inner pipe walls, causing reduced flow and increased pressure on the pump. During the cool season, always perform a full system flush. To do this, open the end caps of the main pipes to allow water to exit at high velocity, carrying away the sediment. This is recommended every 4 to 6 months.

Two-stage filtration

Filters are the first line of defense. If coarse and fine filters are not properly cleaned, particles move toward the 75 mm pipes and may cause blockages in fittings and joints. Always inspect the filter before water enters the main pipes. If you use an automatic flush system, ensure the timing interval is set according to your source water quality. Here we recommend the article on types of drip irrigation tapes examine it to better understand the filtration structure

Pressure management and wear reduction

75-millimeter pipes are designed to withstand irregular pressures or sudden spikes. Installing a pressure regulator at the start of the main line can prevent threaded connections from breaking at junction points. Additionally, loose connections caused by high pressure can lead to leaks and farm under-irrigation.

Using flexible hoses at sensitive points

Where the main line must cross a support or machinery, use flexible hose connectors to prevent impact damage to the rigid 75-millimeter pipe. This is a golden trick for extending service life.

Practical tips for farmers

As a senior reviewer, these empirical tips are for maintenance of 75-millimeter threaded pipes We recommend:

  1. Labeling Branches: Identify each furnace or branch with appropriate labeling so that during repairs, you know which section is isolated.
  2. UV Protection: If the pipe is exposed and not buried, be sure to use protective strips or sun-absorbing coverings.
  3. Clearing the Path: Every year, before the warm season, clear the pipe path of weeds and creeping plants.

In addition to system management, planting programs and farm management are also important. For example, to be informed about other farm variables, you can the seed rate for green onions per hectare to read, as water consumption during peak growth stages of the crop increases pressure on the pipes.

Technical specifications and standards

Standard 75mm pipes must have Iranian National Standard certification. Look for UV Stabilizer (resistant to ultraviolet rays) and nominal pressure (PN) markings on the pipe body. Using non-standard pipes with shorter lifespans forces you to pay replacement costs annually, whereas a quality pipe, with proper maintenance, can last up to 15 years.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Does a 75 mm pipe require thermal insulation in winter?

If the pipe is buried, generally no, except in areas with deep freezing. However, if the pipe is in a greenhouse, freezing temperatures must be prevented; frozen water expands and cracks the pipe.

What is the best method for detecting small fractures?

Use electronic leak detectors. These devices detect the sound of breaking and water leakage. Before piping installation, always perform a Pressure Test.

Can a 75 pipe be connected to a 100 pipe?

Yes, use appropriate reducers and couplers. However, always use flexible connections to reduce shear force at the connection point.

Summary and final recommendation

Caring for water transmission pipes is a long-term investment. By adhering to the principles above, you not only prevent repeated repair costs but also maintain the efficiency of your drip irrigation system. An unmonitored and lead-free system ultimately results in financial losses and water deficiency for plants. We recommend consulting the Cost Guide for a T-Tape System per Hectare to compare with modern solutions and accurately calculate your costs. By regularly following the checklists in this article, your pipes will perform as well as on day one for years to come.
